correctness.rationale: From the projective-plane incidence identity \(BB^T=qI+J\), the four displayed block Fourier eigenvalues follow on constants, bipartition sign, and the two \(\sqrt q\) singular-value spaces. The sign eigenvalue stays negative by the logarithm inequality at all q≥2; the minus branch stays negative. The plus branch is strictly monotone after division by \(2^lpha\) and crosses once at the stated root. Schoenberg centered-Gram rank proves the exact two embedding dimensions; inverse-function Taylor gives the \(q^{-1/2}\) asymptotic. An independent BFS/linear algebra replay on PG(2,p) for p=2,3,5,7 matches the spectrum; finite checks are not substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: The point–line incidence distance hypergroup is a canonical four-class radial harmonic algebra on every projective plane, including planes without transitive symmetry. Its full exponent-dependent nontrivial Fourier-sign spectrum determines a natural sharp negative-type threshold, with a large exact endpoint Hilbert-dimension collapse and a quantitative decay law. This is a complete structural metric classification over an infinite family of geometries, not an arbitrary small numerical slice.
